Recommendation: Once FIDO2 is enabled (see AUTH004), require attestation so only certified, known security key models can be registered. Two documented side effects to plan for, both from Microsoft's own docs. First, CORRECTED 2026-09-09: earlier guidance here said enforcing attestation suppresses the registration campaign nudge entirely - Microsoft's own documentation now states the opposite. Under the Microsoft managed registration campaign state, 'Device-bound with attestation enforced' is itself one of the eligible passkey profile configurations (key restrictions aren't even evaluated for it), so a user in that profile IS nudged - this is an active rollout (Message Center MC1469555, expected complete end of September 2026), so verify directly against the tenant rather than assuming either the old or new behavior. See RCAMP001 for the full corrected eligibility table. Second, synced passkeys do not support attestation at all, so enforcing it also blocks every synced provider regardless of what PASS003 reports. Also worth knowing: attestation is evaluated only at registration time, so turning it on later does not retroactively invalidate passkeys already registered without it - existing weaker registrations need finding and cleaning up separately. Side effect worth knowing about: Microsoft's documented Bluetooth-based cross-device fallback for registering a 'Passkey in Microsoft Authenticator' from a different device than the phone it will live on is explicitly unavailable whenever attestation is enforced. That fallback matters specifically when a new user's Temporary Access Pass is one-time-use and was already consumed reaching Security Info on a laptop, leaving the phone-side registration step with no other way to authenticate (see TAP001 and the New User Bootstrap flow for the full trace). Preferred mitigation is to keep attestation on and use same-device Windows Hello for Business or a short-lived onboarding-only multi-use TAP. If business continuity still requires it, a temporary attestation exception can be used as a controlled transition: time-box it, exclude admin/high-value users, log registrations created during the window, and re-enable attestation on a fixed date with cleanup review.
